What to look for in motorcycle helmets

  • Fit first. The safest helmet is one that fits your head shape snugly with no pressure points — try several brands before buying.
  • Look for ECE 22.06. The current safety standard includes rotational-impact testing. A high SHARP star rating is a useful extra guide.
  • Pinlock-ready visor. Essential for the UK — a Pinlock insert stops fogging on cold, damp mornings.
  • Weight matters. Under ~1,600g keeps neck fatigue down on long days. Composite and carbon shells are lighter than polycarbonate.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on motorcycle helmets?

Our catalogue spans £116.99 to £899.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Arai, Shoei, HJC, Shark, AGV. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Are expensive helmets actually safer?

Not necessarily — every road-legal helmet meets the same ECE 22.06 standard. You pay more for lighter materials, lower noise, better ventilation and comfort features, not a higher safety floor. Always prioritise correct fit.

faq.q: What does ECE 22.06 mean and do I need it?
faq.a: ECE 22.06 is the current European helmet safety standard and it is the one to look for in 2026. It adds rotational-impact testing and tougher checks across more impact points than the older 22.05 rules. Any helmet sold as road legal in the UK must meet an accepted standard, so buy an ECE 22.06 lid and then use the SHARP star rating as a useful extra guide.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a motorcycle helmet?
faq.a: Our shortlist runs from £116.99 to £899.99. Under £150 buys a safe, road-legal helmet with the essentials. The £150 to £400 mid-range, such as the Shoei NXR 2 or HJC RPHA 12, hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers with better ventilation, lower noise and lighter shells. Above £400 you pay for refinement and premium materials, not extra safety.

Not inherently. Every road-legal helmet, from the £116.99 Shark Ridill 2 to the £899.99 Arai RX-7V Evo, meets the same ECE 22.06 safety floor. Spending more buys lighter composite or carbon shells, quieter aerodynamics, better airflow and plusher liners. The safest helmet for you is always the one that fits your head shape snugly with no pressure points.

faq.q: How should a new helmet fit?
faq.a: A correctly sized helmet should feel firm all around with even pressure and no hot spots, and the cheek pads should touch your cheeks. It will loosen slightly as the lining beds in, so avoid a helmet that is roomy when new. Try several brands, as Arai, Shoei, HJC and Shark all use different internal shapes.

faq.q: When should I replace my helmet?
faq.a: Replace a helmet immediately after any significant impact, even if there is no visible damage, because the protective EPS liner crushes on the inside. Otherwise most manufacturers suggest replacement around five to seven years from first use, as sweat, UV and general wear degrade the liner and materials over time.
